title: Reading the headlines
goal: Read Turkish headlines and say what they leave out, and write dates, figures and abbreviations with the right suffix.

intro.text: A headline drops what the reader can rebuild: the copula, often the verb, sometimes the tense. *Benzine zam* is **a price rise for petrol**; *Okullar pazartesi açılıyor* is **schools open on Monday**. Figures and abbreviations take the suffix of the way they are read: *2026'da*, *TDK'ye*.

vocab.en: summary line under a headline (newsroom word)
agenda; the news of the day (gündemde: in the news)

exercises.question: A headline reads *Okullar pazartesi açılıyor*. What does it say?

why.1: With a time word, the headline `-(I)yor` is a near future, not an action going on as you read.

exercises.explain: Headlines announce what is planned with `-(I)yor` and a time word, as English does with **Schools open on Monday**.

accept: A new price rise for petrol
A new price rise for gas
A new price rise for gasoline
A new price rise for fuel
exercises.explain: The dative marks what is affected and the verb is understood: in full, *Benzine yeni bir zam yapıldı*.

exercises.en: In 2026 the rent went up by 15% to 20,000 lira.

reject.why: *2026* is read *iki bin yirmi altı*: the last vowel, ı, is a back vowel, so *'da*.
*Altı* ends in a vowel, so the d of `-DA` stays d: *2026'da*.
*%15* is read *yüzde on beş*: the last vowel is e, so four-way harmony gives *beşlik*: *%15'lik*.
The last vowel of *on beş* is e, a front vowel: *%15'lik*.

exercises.hint: Read each number aloud and harmonize with its last word.
exercises.explain: *2026* → *altı* → *'da*; *%15* → *yüzde on beş* → *'lik*. *20.000 lira* is a word written out, so *liraya* takes no apostrophe.

exercises.question: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: Toplantı Türk Dil Kurumu'nun binasında yapıldı.

why.1: A capital abbreviation takes the suffix that suits its last letter as it is read: *ke*, a front vowel, so *TDK'nin*.
why.2: *Ke* ends in a vowel, so the genitive needs its n: *TDK'nin*.
why.3: The name of an institution written out in full takes no apostrophe: *Türk Dil Kurumunun*.

exercises.prompt: The new metro line opens tomorrow.
accept: Yeni metro hattı yarın hizmete giriyor.
Yeni metro hattı yarın hizmete girecek.
Yeni metro hattı yarın hizmete açılıyor.
Yeni metro hattı yarın hizmete açılacak.
Yarın yeni metro hattı [açılıyor|açılacak|hizmete giriyor|hizmete girecek|hizmete açılıyor|hizmete açılacak].

reject.why: *Açmak* needs an object: someone opens the line. The line itself *açılıyor*.

exercises.explain: Headlines use `-(I)yor` with a time word for what is about to happen; the line is opened, so the verb is passive: *açılıyor*.

exercises.tr: Son dakika: İstanbul'da kar nedeniyle okullar tatil.
exercises.en: Breaking news: schools in Istanbul are closed because of snow.
options: Son dakika: İstanbul'da kar nedeniyle okullar tatil.
Son dakika: İstanbul'da kar nedeniyle okullar açık.
Son dakika: İzmir'de kar nedeniyle okullar tatil.

accept: The governor's office: [Schools|Schools are|Schools will be] [closed|off] tomorrow
Governor's office: Schools will be [closed|off] tomorrow
The governorate: [Schools|Schools are|Schools will be] [closed|off] tomorrow
[The governor's office|Governor's office|Governorate|The governorate]: No school tomorrow
[The governor's office|The governorate] [says|announces|has announced] (that) schools [are|will be] closed tomorrow
exercises.explain: A colon after the speaker introduces their words, and the copula is dropped: in full, *Valilik, okulların yarın tatil olduğunu açıkladı*.

exercises.en: The results will be announced on TÜİK's website at 10 a.m.

reject.why: *10.00* is read *on*: the vowel o is a back vowel, so *10.00'da*.

exercises.explain: *TÜİK* is read as a word, *tüik*, and ends in a consonant: *TÜİK'in*. *10.00* is read *on*: *10.00'da*.

exercises.task: Rewrite each headline as the first sentence of a report would put it: give the verb and the tense the headline leaves out, and end each sentence with a full stop.
exercises.source: Benzine yeni zam / Belediyeden ulaşım açıklaması / Köprü yarın trafiğe kapanıyor
models: Benzine yeni bir zam yapıldı. Belediye, ulaşımla ilgili bir açıklama yaptı. Köprü yarın trafiğe kapatılacak.
Benzinin fiyatı yeniden arttı. Belediyeden ulaşım konusunda bir açıklama geldi. Köprü yarından itibaren trafiğe kapalı olacak.
checklist: *Benzine zam* gets its verb: *zam yapıldı*, or *fiyatı arttı*
The ablative *belediyeden* becomes the subject (*Belediye … açıklama yaptı*) or stays a source (*belediyeden … geldi*)
The headline `-(I)yor` becomes a future: *kapatılacak* or *kapalı olacak*
Each sentence has a finite verb and a full stop
